newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairie seeding 90 pct done June 2 - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairie seeding 90 pct done June 2 - CWB.

text.p: Spring seeding of Canada's six major grains and oilseeds was 90 percent complete by Monday, a Canadian Wheat Board weather analyst said.
"It's going to wrap up here in about a week," CWB weather and crop surveillance director Paul Bullock said.
All wheat seeded area on the Prairies was seen 9.2 percent down at 28.22 million acres in 1997 from 31.08 million acres the year before, Statistics Canada said April 30.
Canola area was forecast to rise 32 percent to 11.585 million acres from 8.8 million, StatsCan said.
StatsCan's next seeding estimate is due June 27.
Alberta was 90 percent planted, Saskatchewan was 91 percent done and Manitoba was 89 percent seeded, he said.
"It's getting to the point where if you haven't got it seeded, intentions are changing. You're down to the last gasps," Bullock added.
The Prairie's grainbelt was forecast to see below normal temperatures between now and June 30, Environment Canada's Winnipeg Climate Centre supervisor Brian Fehr said.
The forecast to the end of August called for normal highs with normal rainfall except in southeast Alberta and southwest Saskatchewan where it may be above normal, Fehr said.
Soil moisture was currently considered dry in the Estevan and Weyburn areas of southeast Saskatchewan, the CWB's Bullock said.
